nodes.name: Ni-Co PBA Coprecipitation
nodes.procedure: Ni-Co PBA (Ni₃[Coᴵᴵᴵ(CN)₆]₂) truncated nanoboxes were prepared as the core by dissolving nickel ion nodes, potassium hexacyanocobaltate(III) linkers, and citrate dihydrate capping agents in deionized water and aging for 24 h.

unit_operations.name: Dissolution
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: dissolving nickel ion nodes, potassium hexacyanocobaltate(III) linkers, and citrate dihydrate capping agents in deionized water

nodes.source_text: Ni-Co PBA (Ni₃[Coᴵᴵᴵ(CN)₆]₂) truncated nanoboxes were prepared as the core by dissolving nickel ion nodes... and aging for 24 h

nodes.name: Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA Core-Shell Formation
nodes.procedure: Ferrous ions were subsequently introduced using the same method [as Ni-Co PBA: dissolving nickel ion nodes, potassium hexacyanocobaltate(III) linkers, and citrate dihydrate capping agents in deionized water and aging for 24 h] to synthesize a Fe-Co PBA (Fe₃[Coᴵᴵᴵ(CN)₆]₂) shell. The solubility product constant (Ksp) of Fe₃[Coᴵᴵᴵ(CN)₆]₂ (Ksp = 2.4 × 10⁻⁴⁰) is smaller than that of Ni₃[Coᴵᴵᴵ(CN)₆]₂ (Ksp = 1.6 × 10⁻¹³), and hence ferrous ions selectively etch the corners of the core Ni-Co PBA (eqs 3 and 4). This resulted in a gradual transformation from a truncated cubic to a spherical core structure. The in situ generated Fe-Co PBA shell wrapped around the spherical core, forming a well-defined core-shell nanobox.

nodes.description: HER performance in alkaline freshwater (1 M KOH)
nodes.source_text: The electrocatalytic performance of the PBA catalysts toward HER was studied by using a standard three-electrode system in 1.0 M KOH... Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA... displayed the best activity (Figure 4a,c, Table S5), showing the lowest overpotentials of 43, 99, and 134 mV to reach the current densities of 10, 50, and 100 mA cm⁻², respectively. The... Tafel slope of 53 mV dec⁻¹... The mass activity of Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA at an overpotential of 60 mV is 43.8 A g⁻¹... The C_dl of Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA is 46.9 mF cm⁻²... Chronoamperometry measurement... no obvious degradation after 100 h test... R_ct... 9.48 Ω in 1 M KOH

nodes.description: HER performance in alkaline simulated seawater (1 M KOH + 0.5 M NaCl)
nodes.source_text: the HER performance of the PBA catalysts was further tested in alkaline simulated seawater (1 M KOH + 0.5 M NaCl) (Figure 4g-h, Table S6)... Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA showed superior catalytic activity... exhibiting the lowest overpotential (η₁₀ = 183 mV, η₅₀ = 233 mV, η₁₀₀ = 258 mV) and Tafel slope (60 mV dec⁻¹)... The stability of Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA in alkaline simulated seawater was also tested by chronoamperometry measurement at an applied potential of -0.23 V versus RHE... the retention rate after 24 h test was 98.4%... R_cts... 10.08 Ω in 1 M KOH + 0.5 M NaCl

nodes.description: Overall water splitting performance in alkaline freshwater (1 M KOH)
nodes.source_text: a water-splitting electrolyzer was set up for overall alkaline freshwater (1 M KOH)... The Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA electrode (cathode) was coupled with... NiCo@A-NiCo-PBA-AA (anode), and nickel foams were used as the substrates... The electrolyzer provided high current densities of 44... mA cm⁻² at a cell voltage of 1.6 V... nearly 100% Faradaic efficiency... lower charge-transfer resistance (R_ct) in freshwater (12.31 Ω)... The stability... tested by chronoamperometry measurement... No obvious attenuation was observed after 100 h test... LSV comparison... after 5000 cycles of CV shows... only slight decay

nodes.description: Overall water splitting performance in alkaline simulated seawater (1 M KOH + 0.5 M NaCl)
nodes.source_text: simulated alkaline seawater (1 M KOH + 0.5 M NaCl) splitting... 30 mA cm⁻² at a cell voltage of 1.6 V... nearly 100% Faradaic efficiency... R_ct... 15.72 Ω... nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-Co PBA shows regular nontruncated cubic structures of uniform size similar to Ni-Co PBA; Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA shows cubic structure with rougher surface and particle size of 230 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b,c displays the FESEM images of NiFe-Co PBA... Figure 1f,g shows the FESEM images of Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA showing a cubic structure similar to that of NiFe-Co PBA, with a relatively rougher surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-Co PBA demonstrates solid structure; Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA clearly shows core-shell structure with spherical core and regular cubic shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and HAADF-STEM images of NiFe-Co PBA are shown in Figure 1d,e, demonstrating its solid structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-Co PBA shows uniform distribution of C, N, Co, Ni, Fe; Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA shows Ni concentrated in core and Fe mainly in shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM-mapping images of NiFe-Co PBA and Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA are displayed in Figure 1j,k, demonstrating that they both are composed of C, N, Co, Ni, and Fe.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-Co PBA indexed to Ni3[Co(CN)6]2 (JCPDS 22-1184); Fe-Co PBA to Fe3[Co(CN)6]2 (JCPDS 46-0907); NiFe-Co PBA peaks between Ni-Co and Fe-Co PBAs; Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA peaks match Fe-Co PBA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a shows the XRD patterns of the PBA-based catalysts. The diffraction peaks of the as-obtained Ni-Co PBA and Fe-Co PBA can be well-indexed as Ni3[Co(CN)6]2...

nodes.characterization_summary: NiFe-Co PBA and Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA show O-H stretching, H-O-H bending, and C≡N stretching modes; Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA shows C≡N redshift to 2176 cm⁻¹ indicating [CoII(CN)6]⁴⁻ formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2b displays the Fourier-transform infrared (FT-IR) spectra of NiFe-Co PBA and Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA. Their main peaks are the same consisting of the O-H stretching mode...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA N content 18.1%; NiFe-Co PBA N content 24.3%; similar Ni, Fe, Co atomic percentages.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The STEM-EDS spectra (Figure 2c) suggest that the N content in Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA (18.1%) is lower than that in NiFeCo PBA (24.3%)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA: 585 m²/g, 1.95 nm pore size; NiFe-Co PBA: 220 m²/g, 0.93 nm pore size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The specific surface area and average pore size (Figure 2d,e) of Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA are 585 m²g⁻¹ and 1.95 nm...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA shows higher C=O/C-C peak ratio and increased distance between peaks; new graphitic N peak with 78% pyridinic+graphitic N; metallic Co peaks from [CoII(CN)6]4- reduction; highest Ni3+ content; significantly increased Fe3+ content.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The fitted C 1s edge spectra (Figure 3a) of the PBA-based catalysts reveal two peaks corresponding to C=O and C-C. The peak ratio of C=O/C-C in trimetallic PBAs is significantly higher... The relative content of Ni3+ is the highest in Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA... the relative content of Fe3+ in Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA is significantly increased

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA shows prominent EPR signal at g=2.005 indicating [CoIII(CN)6]³⁻ vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The prominent electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) signal in Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA at g = 2.005 compared to that of NiFe-Co PBA suggests that [CoIII(CN)6]³⁻ vacancies are generated...

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) calculated from CV: Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA 46.9 mF/cm² (highest ECSA), NiFe-Co PBA 38.2 mF/cm², Ni-Co PBA 20.2 mF/cm², Fe-Co PBA 19.1 mF/cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: ECSA is proportional to the double-layer capacitance (Cdl), which was calculated from the cyclic voltammetry (CV) curve (Figure S5) and shown in Figure 4e. The Cdl of Ni-Co@Fe-Co PBA is 46.9 mF cm⁻²...
